The investigation traced the seed wallet 0xa7f39c1d8e4b2a5f7c3d9e0a1b8c6d4e5f2a67e9 to a network of fourteen distinct blockchain entities through seventeen transfers, reaching a maximum depth of three hops. Sixteen transfers were confirmed, with one inferred correlation, and the fund movement involved rapid automated dispersal within three minutes of receipt, interaction with a mixer contract (transfer of 1,500 USDT to address 0x8589f2c47b1d0a63e95482f7ca1b3d6e0f4a0b6f), and exposure to a cross‑chain bridge (address 0xbb17d4a09e26c35f81b0d7a94e13c68f05b2c530) within two downstream hops. Sixteen of the transfers met or exceeded the 30 % reporting threshold, while one fell below it.

Risk scoring assigned the seed wallet a high score of 65/100, reflecting proximity to a known scam cluster (+20), rapid automated dispersal (+15), mixer interaction (+15) and bridge exposure (+15). The highest‑scoring entity in the chain, address 0x9c04a7e3b21d5f86c0a94e7d2b83f150c6ead21e, received a critical score of 75/100; the seed wallet and address 0x3f1a7d92c04e8b56af10d3e7b829c45d6e0a71bc scored 65/100 and 35/100 respectively.
